title: How many mismatched feature observations can bundle adjustment survive, and does a robust loss help?
lede: with 12 views and wrong camera poses, 2% of observations replaced by random pixels already raise bundle-adjustment surface error from 0.0014 to 0.079 object radii, and Huber or Cauchy loss from the usual all-view start only halve that; a per-point RANSAC start fixes 5% (0.0319) but only 24 views get back to the clean floor at 10% (0.0012). Synthetic only
summary: Follows sensing-ba, whose next step was matching with outliers and a robust loss. On the same synthetic rig (12 views, 0.5 px noise, every pose wrong) a fraction of the observations is replaced by a uniform random pixel. Plain bundle adjustment started from all-view DLT triangulation degrades from 0.0014 (clean) to 0.079 object radii at 2% mismatches and 0.52 at 10%; Huber and Cauchy loss (SciPy least_squares) help only partly (0.027 and 0.043 at 2%, 0.37 and 0.38 at 10%), and trim-and-refit does nothing, because the contaminated all-view triangulation is already a bad start. A per-point RANSAC pair triangulation (20 px gate, wide because the poses are wrong) as the start brings 5% mismatches to 0.032 and, with Cauchy loss, only with 24 views reaches the clean floor at 10% (0.0012 against 0.0010); with 8 to 12 views, where a point is seen in about three, it cannot vote and fails. A robust loss with 40 function evaluations stalled before converging (300 were used). Limits: synthetic, uniform random-pixel mismatches only, known intrinsics, 6 seeds per cell, one gate and loss scale each, not tuned.
